# Kasauti

> Test what you believe about a legal document before you sign it. The user says what they think
> their contract says; Kasauti marks each belief against the document's own words, with a quote and
> page number verified by code rather than by the model.

Kasauti (Hindi, "touchstone") is a Next.js app. Its defining property is the trust boundary: a
language model proposes verdicts and quotes, and deterministic code decides what the user is shown.

## How a check works

1. The user supplies a document (pasted text, an in-browser PDF parse, or a built-in sample).
2. The user picks a situation (tenant, employee, freelancer, consumer).
3. Teach-back: the user writes what they believe the document says, and any promises they were given
   verbally, BEFORE seeing anything quoted from the document.
4. One batched model call returns, per belief: a verdict (backed, contradicted, silent), a verbatim
   quote, search terms, and a one-sentence explanation.
5. Code verifies each quote against the uploaded text (exact, then whitespace/case-normalized, then
   word-level fuzzy above 0.9). Unverifiable quotes are rejected and the verdict becomes
   needs_review with the reason shown. Page and clause numbers are computed from the matched offset.
   A "silent" verdict requires at least two distinct search terms.
6. The report shows verdict cards with evidence, an "ask for this in writing" list (verbal promises
   plus beliefs the document never addresses), questions worth asking a lawyer, and a plain-text
   export.

## Facts

- Verdicts: backed, contradicted, silent, needs_review. Only code can produce needs_review.
- At most two model calls per document (probe questions, then one batched check).
- Degrades to an offline mode with no API key or on any model failure: deterministic probe questions,
  keyword passages, every finding marked needs_review, with a banner stating that nothing was checked.
- Nothing is stored. No database, no analytics. PDFs are parsed on the device; API responses are
  no-store. Live results sit in an in-memory cache for the life of the server instance.
- Quality gate: typecheck, ESLint with zero warnings, Prettier, Vitest at 100% coverage of core, AI,
  server, lib and samples, plus a production build. CI runs the same command.
- Kasauti gives information, not legal advice, and does not assess enforceability in any jurisdiction.
